rename.resolution: Retracted 2026-09-04: the name already agrees. No code change, and no target name invented.

why:
issue 2015 (2026-10-24) -- the key now has a correspondent on our side: `rclcpp_action::create_client<A>(...)` (`rclcpp_action/create_client.hpp`), the ACTION client's free factory, in upstream's node-interface and node shapes, returning `Client<A>::SharedPtr` (`rclcpp::Owned<Client<A>>`, by value, every build). The correlator drops the `rclcpp_action::` prefix, so it lands on this key beside upstream's SERVICE `rclcpp::create_client`, which we still spell as the member `Node::create_client`. ADOPT-BOUNDED: upstream's trailing callback-group / options arguments are not taken, and a failed create aborts naming the action (RFC-0018) where upstream throws.

RETRACTED as a rename 2026-09-04; re-verdicted `divergence`. The row's premise was false BOTH ways, verified: `make_client` has never existed anywhere in the tree (`git grep make_client -- packages examples book` is empty), and `nros::create_client` HAS existed since 61ce91c25 (2026-03-11), at `std_compat.hpp:145` in the since-DELETED header, alongside the member `Node::create_client<S>` (`node.hpp:477`). The row proposed renaming FROM a name never written TO a name already in use.

Issue 0818's blind spot produced it: the since-DELETED `std_compat.hpp` sat behind `#ifdef NROS_CPP_STD`, which the extractor did not define, so its eleven free functions were invisible. `api-parity.py:141-147` records the same cause producing the `make_publisher` -> `create_publisher` rename against an already-existing `nros::create_publisher`. These rows were written in that pass and not revisited when `CPP_TRANSLATION_UNITS` fixed the extractor.

What actually differs is SHAPE, and it is three RFC constraints rather than a name: rclcpp takes three `node_interfaces::*Interface` shared_ptrs and returns a throwing `SharedPtr`; ours takes `Node&` with an out-param and `Result` — no interface decomposition (RFC-0022), no allocator, no exceptions (RFC-0018/0036).

phase-442 W2 (2026-09-11) — `std_compat.hpp` is DELETED, so any sentence above naming that header describes a spelling that no longer exists. It was a third orphaned vocabulary: free functions shadowing the `Node` methods a ported file calls, dead in every shipping configuration, and RFC-0096 removed the layer it belonged to. The always-available spelling is the method.
